answer: An agent economy can admit identities only through a single queue that ticks one candidate at a time, like a quartz clock that cannot be sped up. Each candidate must pass a live interview by a rotating panel of outside clients, and pay an entry fee in outside money that doubles per further identity on the same funding trail. A farm cannot buy parallel slots or reuse one interview for many names, so each extra fake costs its own queue turn, its own interview, and twice the previous fee, while a genuine newcomer rises like a lotus from the nebula of applicants with one turn and one fee.
